name: Device-side assert guard
description: A device-side assert(gtid < N) compile-in guard; the launch is intentionally larger than N so a known subset of threads trip the assert (cudaErrorAssert), while a counterpart kernel records the same predicate as a 0/1 flag per thread.
output_description: CUDA executable writes numeric output to output/cuda_output.txt.

performance.notes: Runtime logs are written by tools/benchmark_case.py.

extraction_notes: testKernel reproduced verbatim from NVIDIA/cuda-samples simpleAssert.cu. testKernelFlag (numeric-oracle counterpart), host driver, CMakeLists, and Python oracle are new. Snapshot sk-06.
notes: Real-extraction device-assert case from collection snapshot sk-06. N=1000, total=1024 threads -> first 1000 flags are 1, remaining 24 are 0. Part 2 trips the device assert on purpose (expected stderr diagnostics; sticky error cleared, process returns 0).
